_comment: Round-10 fix wave (Phase 3). Inputs: ISSUES.json and JUDGE.json on handoff/audit-r10-register (PR #2244, head d23205d13); CATCHUP-JUDGE.json at 33ffa7aa9; issues #2219-#2243; the orchestrator's plan (owner-reported, study, instrument and arch groups).

One entry per pull request. Grouped by class first, then classes touching the same owning seam merged; a group that would span more than one owning module is split, so a class issue can sit in several groups. `fixes` names the issues a group closes because it is the deepest group holding them (wave depth); the body says Part of for the rest. Where two holders are unordered and the deeper one merges first, the orchestrator moves the closing keyword to the last merge and verifies the close.

Every group holds at least one filed issue. The 22 group issues from dev/audit/rounds/round10/ROSTER-ISSUES.json (#2252-#2273) and the four class issues N-leaf-imports-solver, N-restore-race, N-order-coupling and N-solve-recompute (#2247-#2250) are wired into `issues`; no pending token remains. The roster check: no group without an issue, and no open round-10 issue without a group.

`files` is the conflict map's input and `after` serialises every pair of groups sharing a file, except the shared test and record files every group appends to (tests/features.py, tests/entities.py, tests/seam_map.json, tests/finite_boundary.py, tests/guard_pins.py, tests/dst_checks.py, tests/arch_score_head.py, tests/structure_budgets.json, the mutation ledger): a conflict there is a rebase the fixer seat resolves at its own merge base, re-deriving every budget figure.
Hot files (const.py, coordinator.py, optimizer.py, config_flow.py, the card script) carry an architect note in each group's brief (orchestrator.md section 5, fixer.md step 17).

Ordering rules applied: high and critical first; structure-reducing groups before code-adding ones; defect fixes before the large arch moves on the same files; the deep-link helper before UX-SETUP, UX-HEALTH and ADVISOR; RATIO-SITES before SCORES, the identifiability groups and TRUST-RELATIVE; HEAT-METER before COP-GATE; ARCHSCORE-COVERAGE before the D7 M7/M8 policy fold (R10-BRIEFS-FOLD).

`wave` is the dependency depth (1 = startable now). `size` is S/M/L/XL by diff and seam count. `severity` is the judge's (catch-up judge where it re-rated); owner-reported, study and instrument groups carry no judge rating and are entered as medium unless the owner said otherwise.

D12-s3-01 (high, verified; the judge merged D7-s6-91 into it by perturbation-cross both ways, 42.222 K to 0.000 K, nulls 0) delivers 2 of 6 cells wrong on a degF install. The root fix is ARCH3-s6 patch P2, the set-point I/O owner in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/inputs.py, at 532d8d09d: `dev/audit/rounds/round10/D7/arch3-s6/patches/P2_setpoint_io_owner.patch`. ARCHITECT NOTE AMENDED (orchestrator, 2026-10-19, mandate 6175172275, on the round-2 review of #2391): the Shape clause "a detector input independent of the replay residual" is satisfied by the detector folding the residual's departure from a tracked reference (level plus heat and sun slopes, fitted by forgetting least squares), because a steady, heat-scaled or sun-scaled model bias cannot move that departure once the fit converges. A residual input with a tracked reference is accepted in place of an independent input. The known transient while the sun slope converges is routed to R10-NIGHT-FOLDS's carry with its control.

carry: From R10-VENT-DETECTOR (#2241): `_async_learn_house_heat_loss` feeds the open-window CUSUM (`self._vent_cusum.update(now, float(residual), (previous_power * dt_h, (previous_state.solar_radiation or 0.0) * dt_h / 1000.0))`) before its `HOUSE_LOSS_MAX_RESIDUAL` rejection, and the detector measures each residual against a forgetting least-squares fit on that heat input and sun. A night-interval predicate must sit AFTER that call: gating the feed by daylight starves the detector by day (it force-releases after `VENT_CUSUM_STARVE_HOURS`) and hides from its fit the power and sun range the day spans. Control: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_vent_bias_window.py` at the fold's merge base and head -- `false_share` stays 0.000 on the delivery 1.0 / UA 1.0 / no-window arm and the wide (300 W/K) planted windows keep `detect_h` finite on all 20 arms, as they do at this group's head. When the owner's bundle is re-measured after this group lands, report the vent freeze share (intervals `_learning_frozen` returns "ventilation") beside the UA figures.

From #2391: a sun-scaled bias trips the detector while its sun slope converges (the scratch probe under `## Figures`: 27 and 107 tripped 15-min intervals over four days at 0.4 and 1.0 K), the same aperture residual as the finder's P1 fix2.00 arms. From R10-THERMAL-POWER-OPTION (#2753; finding-propagation.md), superseding this brief's opening premise. Your energy meter is a second heat source beside this one: state which of the two wins when both are configured, keep that no-fallback rule (a configured source whose reading is unusable never falls back to another), and route your reading through `read_heat_output_kw` rather than a parallel path. The house learner already replays measured heat (`_interval_measured_heat_kw`, `_replay_interval`), and `flow_meter.replay_freeze` lifts the (c) unmetered-power freeze for a heat-metered interval on switch-plus-setpoint installs. That lift decides space against hot water only from the commanded split (`_commanded_split`), never from an observed pump mode, so a meter that also counts the pump's self-initiated hot-water charges is replayed as space heat on exactly the installs the freeze protected (a judgement on the code, not measured on a plant). Your mode split ('split delivered heat ... by the heat-pump mode entity') must therefore apply to the thermal power entity's reading and to this replay as well as to your energy meter's. Control: #2753's check 'a configured heat meter answers in kW, and outranks the flow meter's estimate' fails when `read_heat_output_kw`'s `if cap.measured_heat:` is mutated to `if False:` (review 2753 mutant M1); keep it passing, and add the same check for your source's precedence.

Owner request (tvofi, 2026-10-15). Main has no delivered-heat energy input: the only heat-output path is `CONF_FLOW_METER_ENTITY` (`read_heat_output_kw` in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/flow_meter.py), used only without a power and a frequency signal. The mode entity is REQUIRED when the heat meter is configured, with a refusal if it is missing. Guards: counter resets and rollover; interval alignment between the two meters; a minimum delta so quantisation does not dominate; hot-water intervals get their own COP bin and never feed the space learner.

Three seams. (1) `_cop_reference_curve`/`_commanded_split` (custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py:4482-4852) pick the curve from the plan's split as the mode can serve it, not from the duty the pump actually ran; the pump-duty ledger records it ran hot water the plan did not command (11 `dhw-instead` steps in the published day), so a pump-initiated hot-water run folds against the space curve and the space ask. Refuse a fold whose observed duty differs from the planned duty. (2) `MeasuredCop.record` (accuracy.py:873) latches one interval and `ObservedCOPSensor` (sensor.py:1670) publishes it with no age while every later interval is refused (`last_refusal` `duty_floor`); show the sample's time or the honest not-measurable state this group adds. (3) The accuracy residual (coordinator.py:9901-9924) re-subtracts the latched COP on every sample, so 89 consecutive samples carry a residual that is a pure function of outdoor temperature. Controls: a synthetic install whose pump runs unplanned hot water folds nothing for those intervals; a draw-follows-plan install still folds (your existing null); one mutant per seam. [implemented: 14ed13551]

Correction to the D15 triage carry on the observed-COP latch (2026-10-24; derived ratios only). Seam (1) of the earlier carry, a hot-water run folded against the space curve, is withdrawn. The bundle has no mode history for the interval (the pump-duty ledger is not persisted and starts 17 h later), but the code rules DHW-only out. The stored record says `curve_dhw` False, and a commanded ask of 1.26 kW folded. Under an observed DHW-only mode, `_commanded_split` (coordinator.py:4482-4511) zeroes space, so a space-curve fold with that ask is impossible: the interval ran in a space-capable mode. Real cause: the arbiter commanded a 44-46 degC flow set-point, and the pump drew 2.30x the plan's kW to meet it. The fold reads ask over draw as efficiency (COP-GATE's premise). The ask was under the nameplate third (1.26 against 1.33 kW), so `judge_ratio` (accuracy.py:844-871) could only fold through `follows_ask` returning True. That evidence window is misaligned. `draw_range.fold` runs in `_record_accuracy` (coordinator.py:9838), called at :5670 after `async_run_optimization` (:5634) has adopted the next action, so it pairs the closed interval's meter with the next step's ask. Of the 32 stored draw samples, 14 match the next accuracy row's ask, 0 match the same row's, and 15 are ambiguous (a constant ask). The COP fold itself (:6494, before the solve) and the accuracy pairing are aligned. Fix the pairing, then re-judge `follows_ask`. Seams (2), the latch with no age, and (3), the residual reusing the latch, stand. Controls: a synthetic install whose draw follows a flow set-point and not the kW ask folds nothing; the draw window pairs each meter reading with its own step's ask (mutation: swap to the next step); your existing draw-follows-plan null still folds. [implemented: 14ed13551]

Repair, without lengthening the lease (P206 rejected that arm) and without changing `renew()`'s refusals: in the `flock-wrap` path, when the recorded owner is still this label and has expired and no other label's ticket waits, refresh it; when the owner is gone or another's, or another label waits, take again at the back of the queue exactly as `RenewRefused` already does (`:861-877`), instead of failing the command. carry: From R10-SAV-BASELINE (#2255, PR #2411): the month row's flat-price null reads 10.83 % saved at that head (43.66 % at its base) by `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_baseline.py`. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_null_terms.py` splits the 13.9 kWh gap (booked thermostat 128.4, plan 114.5) into three terms, and the acceptance must separate them, not drive the null to 0. (a) Comfort: 6.6 kWh, about 5 of the 10.83 points; the plan holds 18.79 °C against a 20.44 °C mean target; a comfort-matched baseline or a priced comfort shortfall answers it. (b) COP timing: power-weighted COP +17.27 % at a flat price, because the plan heats in the warmer hours; this is a real saving and must survive. (c) Stored heat: +23.7 kWh_th (about 13.3 kWh_e) left unsettled by the 2-day window; the month row does not settle it, `predicted_savings` does. Control: the harness's `const` arm (outdoor at the window mean) reads timing +0.00 % and gap 15.6 = comfort 5.1 + start drawdown 10.1. Acceptance: with comfort matched, the `const` arm with stored heat settled at both ends (or a window long enough) reads about 0, and the varying-outdoor arm reads the timing term, not 0. Second limit: the start-of-horizon settlement is capped by the thermostat's space-heat cost, and that leaves `summer_dhw_only` at -12.74 % predicted savings (-3.17 % on main; -0.27 SEK on a 2.09 SEK reference), because the summer house starts above the end's comfort caps. Settled at the caps alone it read 1.95 %, but `away_setback` then read 60.71 %. Re-measure both at your merge base.

From the D15 production triage of the owner's 7.0.4 diagnostics bundle (2026-10-24; derived ratios only, the bundle stays out of every ref): the open month's savings are negative by volume, not by price timing. The booked thermostat baseline (`add_savings_settlement`, custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/ledger.py:195-228, fed by `current_action["baseline_kw"]` from optimizer.py:5689) is a modelled electric kWh, while `savings_actual` is metered kWh (spot plus immersion); the month's baseline kWh is 0.384x its metered kWh, and the plan's own prediction under-reads the meter 1.56x over the 192-sample accuracy window, 17.8 % of metered draw falling in intervals the plan predicted at zero (pump-initiated hot water). Flat-price null: pricing both sides at one price leaves 95-102 % of the negative month (volume term -94.5 %, timing term -5.5 %), so the owner-required null "savings about 0 on a flat-price profile" fails on volume before any comfort or stored-heat separation is reached. The baseline and the actual must be compared on one basis: both modelled, or the baseline scaled by the same meter calibration (`accuracy.power_ratio`), with draw the plan never commanded classified rather than charged to the plan. Controls: the flat-price null reads about 0 on a synthetic install whose meter exceeds the model by a fixed factor; a no-gap install keeps today's figures byte-identical; one mutant. Harness shape: recompute volume and timing terms from `ledger.months[<month>].lines` (synthetic bundle only in-tree). [implemented: 34cd75bf1]

Correction to the D15 triage carry on savings volume (2026-10-24; derived ratios only). The earlier text called the draw in plan-zero intervals "pump-initiated hot water". That is wrong: the integration owns the mode. The cause is the integration's own DHW handling. Re-derived from the 57-step pump-duty ledger (`pump_arbiter._observe`/`_verdict`, custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py:1001-1038): 3 of 4 planned one-step DHW slots show no run inside the slot, and 7 of 8 plan-idle steps within three steps after a slot ran. Null control: plan-idle steps with no DHW slot in the previous three steps ran 4 of 41, and 3 of those 4 continue one DHW run. Seam: an idle row writes no mode (`desired`, pump_arbiter.py:700-707), so the DHW mode written for the slot stays on through the idle steps. The pump then starts late and charges to its own set-point, while the plan booked one 15-minute slot. Over the 192 accuracy rows: 10 of the 13 running rows in plan-zero intervals sit next to a planned-on step, which is start and run-on lag. The plan's kW for its own commanded steps reads 1.28x low, because the arbiter commands a flow set-point and not a kW. Standby is refuted (median 0.0 kW in idle rows). Immersion (3.9 % of the month's actual kWh) is in `savings_actual` (ledger.py:225) but has no counterpart in the thermostat baseline. Owner acceptance (binding on this group): the corrected monthly savings must equal what the card's Savings tab shows. Today the card reads `MonthlySavingsSensor.extra_state_attributes["savings_months"]` (sensor.py:487-525, card `_savingsPageHtml`), which is `ledger.savings_months` (coordinator.py:7864, ledger.py:332). Main's code over the bundle's ledger store gives a Savings cell equal to the sensor's state, by construction. The divergences the owner sees are in the same tab and header. (a) The header's "Projected savings" (`_plan_predicted_savings`, a plan-horizon figure) is positive while the month row is negative. (b) The row's Baseline and Actual columns are on a bill basis (capacity, wear and immersion, ledger.py:302 `month_cost`), while its Savings cell is a spot-energy difference. So Baseline is 3.49x the thermostat's booked cost, and the % column divides one basis by the other. Fix in `ledger.savings_months` only, so that the tab, the sensor state and the closed-month receipt's saved line read one figure on one basis. Pin it with a test that renders the card's Savings page from the sensor payload and asserts each cell equals `ledger.savings_months`. [implemented: 34cd75bf1]

Owner specification for the savings baseline (tvofi, 2026-10-24, binding acceptance criterion). Actual consumption is calculated from the heat pump's power sensor. The baseline must use power levels similar to the ones recorded, simulated as a plain thermostat over the exact same price profile, for both space heating and DHW. The DHW baseline assumes the DHW thermostat is always on: no DHW windows. Savings are the cost of that baseline minus the metered actual cost, priced over the same profile. Under one flat price, the volume difference may remain, but timing savings must be 0. The card's Savings tab equals ledger.savings_months cell for cell. Replace the modelled-thermostat volume (_thermostat_held_state, optimizer.py:358; baseline at 0.38x metered) with this definition.

Correction to carry-d15-sav-volume-2 (D15 triage, 2026-10-24; derived ratios only). Withdrawn: "an idle row writes no mode, so the DHW mode keeps the pump charging through plan-idle steps". The owner's integration also owns the supply switch, and the ledger statistic it rested on, 7 of 8 idle steps after a DHW slot ran, is not evidence that the pump ran outside a planned slot. Three seams. (1) The ledger freezes `planned` at the step's first one-minute tick (`_observe`, custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py:1006-1010). That is the plan from before the mid-step re-solve, and the re-solve can move a DHW slot onto the current step. In the bundle, the 13:00 row reads planned dhw while the 13:13 solve's action for that same step is space 0.5 kW and dhw 0. `ran` is real metered pump draw of at least `on_threshold_kw` (0.25 kW) on any one-minute pass (pump_arbiter.py:1013-1015). `dhw` is the mode flag or a tank rise (pump_arbiter.py:1020-1026). (2) The arbiter never writes the switch (pump_arbiter.py:46). The switch is written once per coordinator cycle, from the new plan's step 0 (`_apply_action`, coordinator.py:7581-7595, after the solve at :5634). Cycles run every 15.39 min (median of 641) against 15-minute steps, at a phase spread uniformly through the step (quartiles 4.3, 8.2 and 11.4 min). So each switch-on lasts into the next step, and a slot written late in its own step starts the compressor in the following one: 3 of 4 planned DHW slots show no run in-slot. (3) Checked and refuted: the solve's switch schedule disagreeing with its ask. 0 of 672 published steps were switched on without an ask, or off with one. The bundle holds no switch-state history, so "switch commanded off while draw continued" can be neither confirmed nor ruled out. Owed: score each ledger step against the plan in force when the step's actuation happened (re-freeze `planned` at each cycle's adoption), and actuate the switch at step boundaries, from the arbiter's one-minute tick, rather than at the cycle phase. Controls: a synthetic install with the cycle phase at 0 and at 14 min books identical duty verdicts; a step whose plan changed mid-step is scored against the plan that actuated it; one mutant per seam. The card-equality acceptance from carry-d15-sav-volume-2 stands. [implemented: 5d4e0bcfb]

groups.brief: On installs whose pump power is set through a heating-flow setpoint behind a buffer tank and mixing valve, the setpoint is a power command (owner, 2026-10-19: a 55 degree setpoint in short slots applies maximum power while the system volume rises slowly). Two defects keep the plan at the minimum level all day despite price spread. (1) flow_setpoint_for_level maps the minimum level to the return temperature (35 C without a return sensor), which on a 23-34 C tank yields about a third of the planned draw. Heat-pump outgoing and return temperatures become optional config inputs, and leaving them unset keeps current behaviour exactly. Carried from #2465 (R10-SETPOINT-BOOST) at afabd5b6; the ceiling probe owns these:
- **The mapping reads the water temperature only at the floor.** The floor is relative to the inlet, the ceiling is absolute, and the levels between are linear in configured power. A pump's draw follows the set-point minus the water temperature, and it saturates. So the same level commands a different power at every tank temperature, and the gain between set-point and draw is unidentified on a set-point-driven install. Identifying that gain is R10-CEILING-PROBE's: its cheap-night `sysid.py` experiment measures drawn power against the commanded set-point. The booked-vs-delivered heat that follows from the gap is R10-DEMAND-OVERBOOK's, carried under `## Forward-carry`.
- **Reaching the real maximum** needs either p_max configured at its true value (an owner question for tvofi, who is adjusting the config) or a deliberate ceiling probe. The probe is R10-CEILING-PROBE, folded into the cheap-night system-identification experiment (`sysid.py`). B is its prerequisite: the window now admits ceiling-commanded evidence only.
- **Idle draw can absorb compressor draw.** If the gate is not truly off (the compressor runs at the gate on a cold inlet), the learned idle median takes in compressor draw. carry: The stuck andon must report stalled progress, not elapsed time (P211/V131, from three healthy pushes it raised: #2876 pid 85023 at 2295 s, #2854 pid 55046 at 1919 s while its whole tree advanced +3.4 s CPU per 20 s, and pid 19711 at about 37 min). `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh`'s `stuck_arm()` reports any `upd-*.lock` held past `HPO_PUSH_STUCK_SECS` (900) -- but a dead holder's flock is released by the kernel, so it can only ever report a live run, and `tests/gate_lock.py:53-56` records that a prepr routinely runs past 1800 s. Keep the 900 s age floor; report a lock past it only when the summed utime+stime of its recorded run pid's process tree (the descendants of field 1 of the lock file, `pr_args.sh:85`) has not advanced by more than 0.2 s between two consecutive passes; the first sighting past the bound stores the sample and prints nothing (one pass of delay, never less); sample the tree, not the pid, because the holder sleeps in a 0.2 s poll (`pr_args.sh:102`) and the run's shell waits on its child; an unreadable sample keeps today's line with `cpu=?`, so the change cannot silence the alarm where it cannot measure; the line keeps its shape and gains the delta (`STUCK <branch> <pid> <age>s cpu+<delta>`), and says "no CPU advance", not "hung", because a push waiting on I/O is flat too; a released lock is never read, unchanged. REJECTED in the same ruling: raising the threshold and lengthening `gate_lock`'s lease -- a prepr takes a pool slot held for the life of its run, not the exclusive lease (`tests/gate_lock.py:53-56`), and the lease covers only the machine-measuring scripts (recorded at 936.3 s and 241.1 s against 1800). Fold (e) of #1930, deferred as high risk and lost: #1975 closed #1930 with (a)-(d), the words survive only inside the done group R9-F10.16's brief, and nothing in round 10 names it (found by the 2026-10-20 slip screen). The option, verbatim: skipping a driver on a mutant line it never executes. In practice the mutation lane runs every driver against every mutant, and a driver whose tests never reach the mutated line cannot kill it, so those runs are pure cost; skipping them saves CI time with the same killing power. The risk is asymmetric: one wrong skip loses a real killer, the mutant survives, and the lane either reports a false survivor or hides a genuine test gap -- which is why the deferral demanded a 595-row replay. Build it measure-first, in this order, and do not reorder: (1) build the 595-row replay -- for every mutant/driver pair, record from a real run whether that driver executes the mutated line, and land the matrix as a checked-in artifact with its command; (2) enable a skip only where a matrix row says the driver never reaches the line -- no skip may be enabled without its row, and a pair with no row must run; (3) prove with a null control that the kill set under skipping is identical to the kill set without it on the whole matrix, and that the survivor set is unchanged. If the matrix shows no pair is skippable, record that measurement and stop: the answer is then a recorded refusal, not a feature. The 595 figure is the row count from #1930's harness at that head -- re-derive it, do not carry it.

Triage P-A (s4, batch 3, 2026-10-22, accepted narrowed), verbatim:
## P-A Cloud dispatch payload size: render a stub that points at a pushed ref

VERDICT: ACCEPT NARROWED -> R10-FLOW-DESIGN-STAGES (not-started, M, no `after`, files already include
tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py). Plus a cleanup carry to R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS (not-started).

Measured facts:
- The ref half is already on main. R10-FLOW-DISPATCH is done. `dispatch_group()` / `--role R --group G --model M`
  publishes PAYLOAD.json and PROMPT.md as `dispatch/<role>-<topic>` and prints the ref name. INSTRUMENTS.md says "fire
  the standing trigger with the printed ref". 19 `dispatch/*` refs exist on origin.
- The missing piece: nothing renders the short trigger body. The ccr is resent whole on every trigger update (INSTRUMENTS.md,
  "every trigger update resends the full ccr"), so a standing trigger still needs a ccr whose prompt names the ref. Today
  the only output is the full ccr or the bare ref name. No `--stub` or equivalent exists (grep of cloud_dispatch.py).
- Volume: cloud-sessions.tsv has 35 fires on 2026-10-22. Brief plus carries of not-started roster groups: median 2.4 KB,
  max 28.9 KB, so the saving is concentrated in the large briefs (P2b-class), not the median.
- Not re-measured: the orchestrator's "about 35k tokens for 11 KB". 11 KB is about 3k tokens per copy, so 3 echoes is
  about 9k; 35k implies roughly 12 copies. Treat the figure as unverified; the direction holds at either number.
Ref-family cleanup cost (the question asked): a stub adds no new ref, since it reuses `dispatch/*`. But
prune_refs.py has no `dispatch/` or `brief/` rule (grep: only handoff/, verdict/, ci-probe/, archive/), so these refs are
residue that nothing deletes. 19 dispatch refs now, about 35 a day at the 10-22 rate, and 1 `brief/*` ref. R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS
carry (ii) already guards "dispatch/* younger than 24h", which presumes a delete rule that is not there.
Cost: S inside an M group on the same file; one `--stub` arm, a self-test arm with null control (full ccr unchanged byte for byte),
a mutant. Benefit: orchestrator tokens per fire, 35 fires a day.

Verdict: ACCEPT-narrowed: hold on a git-read merge verdict at the head, not on `review/<pr>` or an APPROVED review.
Reason: claim verified. At origin/main tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh the handoff arm (loop at lines 238-248) skips a PR only when the handoff/body refs are absent, the handoff is already an ancestor of the head (`merge-base --is-ancestor`), the PR number is in `<state>/cloud-handoff-hold` (line 244, HELD), or `<topic> <sha>` is in the failed record. It reads neither a verdict nor an approval; it then runs update_pr.sh, which merges the handoff and origin/main into the head (update_pr.sh:55-57) and so moves it. The hold file exists (R10-FLOW-RELAY-HOLD, done) but only the orchestrator writes it, so the protection depends on someone listing #2651 before the beat; nothing derives it. Two corrections to the proposal: (1) `review/<pr>` is the review DISPATCH commit; the verdict is on `verdict/<pr>` (origin/verdict/2645's tip subject reads `verdict: #2645 Fix review: merge <40-hex>`), so the condition is: `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/verdict/<pr>`, fetch the tip, subject `Fix review: merge <head>` where `<head>` equals the PR's current head. That is git-only; an APPROVED-review check needs a per-PR `gh` read each 5-minute pass over up to 100 PRs, so drop it (a merge verdict at the head is what an approval is conditioned on, and a verdict naming a different head is already void). (2) The hold prints `HELD` but is silent on why; the new case prints `HELD-VERDICT #<pr> <handoff tip>` once per pass, and also lands a level line so the tick reports it as a decision for main, not a failure. Open risk: for a fix PR, a new fixer handoff ahead of a merge-verdicted head is genuine new work that must void the verdict, so the hold cannot be permanent; main releases it by removing the verdict's staleness (dispatching a re-review) or listing the PR in the hold file's inverse. The fixer picks the release (suggest: the report line names `bus.sh dispatch` as the next step). A handoff updates only with the body pushed for it (V147). (a) `tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh` adds a trailer line `Code: <40-hex>` to the body commit's message (`commit-tree -m`, :73). (b) In `cloud_relay.sh`'s `handoff_arm`, after it fetches `handoff-body/<topic>` and before it runs `update_pr.sh`, it reads that tip's message. If the message has a `Code:` line naming a sha other than `hs`, it does not update: it writes `level_line handoff-body-stale refs/heads/handoff/<topic> <hs>` with why `body names <sha12>` and retries on the next pass, with no `cloud-handoff-failed` entry. groups.brief: adopt one arm only, as new fly-in R10-FLY-ROW-HEAD-CARRY (S/M, lane F, code-owned .github/workflows/*: cite mandate approval 6319294694), with after-edges R10-CI-LAYOUT-P2 and R10-FLY-OPENPR-ATOMIC. The arm: carry the previous head's completed Tests, CodeQL, Hassfest and Validate results to a head whose diff from that head is exactly the PR's own dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md. Decline every path-filter skip and every policy, docs or fixture .md relaxation -- measured from one bulk Actions listing (5 calls of up to 1000 runs, 2026-10-21 00:00-21:00Z; 3 windows capped at 1000, so this is a sample) and git diffs between consecutive PR heads. "run-min" is a run's started-to-updated wall time, not billed job minutes. (1) Shares, over 116 consecutive PR-head pairs and 11066 PR run-min: 47 heads add only merges from main (3889 run-min), 10 carry code (1417), and 59 are .md-only (2399, 21.7%). All 59 .md-only heads are the record class: delivery rows only. Policy, docs and fixture .md heads number 0, so relaxing them buys nothing. For docs and fixtures the scoped gate already runs 0 scripts, and policy .md must always run policy_lint and the code-owner rule. (2) The record class comes in two shapes. (a) record/autofix PRs: 37 heads, 579 run-min (5.2%), whose Tests already run scoped (about 3.8 min a head). A job-level path skip of the code-only workflows would save about 290 run-min (2.6%), but it makes required contexts report a skipped success with no run behind it, which is a weaker guarantee than any run. Declined. (b) open_pr.sh's second push, the row-only head: 22 heads, 1820 run-min on the row heads (16.4%), plus 1277 on the code heads it superseded. Only 3 of 22 superseded heads finished Tests; the rest were cancelled by concurrency. The gap between the two heads has a median of about 8 min and a tail of 198 and 500 min (refused second pushes, P13's class). The PR's whole diff is code, so a path filter can skip nothing here. Only a carry keyed on the head-diff can avoid the re-run. The writer-side fix (one push) is impossible because the row's name needs the PR number. Moving the row out of the PR changes delivery-status-tracking.md (policy, moratorium 0012). (3) The carry. No cancel when the superseding head's diff is exactly delivery/<N>.md of this PR. The row head's Tests, CodeQL, Hassfest and Validate contexts post head1's completed conclusions under the same check names and app, so the ruleset is unchanged. Governance (record, delivery-status, policy-docs) and PR contract are never carried and always run. Estimated saving: about 49 run-min per opened PR (today about 3097 run-min for 22 opens; after the carry, about 2020), about 10% of PR CI, plus about 8 min of lead time per open (CI finishes at T, not gap+T). (4) Ordering. After R10-CI-LAYOUT-P2, because the same workflow files are under a design-approved consolidation into one umbrella required check, which leaves one context to mirror instead of four, and the P2 ruleset cut-over is the orchestrator's. After R10-FLY-OPENPR-ATOMIC, which removes the 198 and 500 min refused-second-push tail. No open PR overlaps beyond #2585 (CI-LAYOUT-P1, tests.yml, governance.yml). (5) Null control (fixtures in the fly-in's self-test, plus one live planted head on a throwaway PR): a row-only head-diff carries. Row plus a one-byte CLAUDE.md edit does not carry, and policy-docs (policy_lint) goes red. Row plus a new unclassified .md does not carry, and Tests' entities goes red ("these force the FULL suite when touched"). A row for another PR's number, or a body the contract refuses, does not carry, and PR contract and delivery-status go red. A carried head whose head1 failed carries the failure, never a success. Triage P-B (s4, batch 3, 2026-10-22, accepted), verbatim:
## P-B tick_loop.sh runs stale code: freshness check

VERDICT: ACCEPT -> R10-FLY-RELAY-REVIEW-FF (not-started, S, files include tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh and cloud_relay.sh),
plus a forward-carry to R10-ORCH-MACHINERY's design (finding-propagation) because the same hazard moves to beatd.py.

Measured facts (origin/main tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh):
- It does no self-check at all. No `git` call, no SHA, no version in the banner or the heartbeat message. Each pass runs
  `$HERE/cloud_relay.sh pass` and `$HERE/orchestrator_tick.py` from whatever checkout it started in; only `tick_loop.sh` itself is
  read once. So a checkout never updates and every fix to those files is invisible to a running loop.
- The stale checkout 16a8240f1 (2026-10-22 08:11 +0200) is 506 commits behind origin/main fef4a1351; 119 touch tools/audit/seat and
  28 touch cloud_relay.sh, tick_loop.sh or orchestrator_tick.py. The hold check landed in cfa89d24f (R10-FLOW-RELAY-HOLD).
  A path filter on tools/audit/seat therefore cuts the restart rate from 506 to 119 candidates.
- Ownership: no group owns it. R10-RCA-ORCH-CONTINUITY and R10-FLOW-ANDON (tick_loop.sh, both done) cover liveness (heartbeat), not
  code freshness, so the heartbeat reads healthy while the code is old. R10-ORCH-MACHINERY (L, not-started) moves the relay to a
  launchd-supervised beat; its brief has no clause on which checkout the beat runs, so the hazard would carry over. FLY-RELAY-REVIEW-FF
  and R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN are the not-started groups on tick_loop.sh; REVIEW-FF is S and sits on the relay_start lines.
Design (narrower than the proposal):
- Do not fast-forward by default. The loop is documented as a read-only driver, and orch-wt is a worktree other seats may share
  (a dirty tree or a detached HEAD would make `merge --ff-only` fail or surprise).
- Each pass: `git -C $HERE fetch -q origin main` (a git fetch, no API) and count `HEAD..origin/main -- tools/audit/seat`. Put
  `code=<sha7> behind=<N>` in the TICK-PASS banner and the heartbeat message, so staleness shows off-host.
- If behind>0 and the tree is clean and `merge --ff-only` succeeds: `bash -n` the new tick_loop.sh, then `exec bash "$0" "$@"`. Otherwise
  print `TICK-STALE behind=N` and carry on (never exit: a stopped loop is worse than a stale one).
Null control: a throwaway origin whose main did not move prints behind=0 and does not exec. Mutant: drop the path filter or the
`bash -n` guard. Cost: S; one fetch per 300 s pass, 288 a day, no API.
Binding constraints: tick_loop.sh is measured by the mutant file (new arm takes a per-file id, e.g. tick_loop-N); a new git call
sites need no PUSHERS entry (fetch only). The exec guard matters: a broken main would crash-loop the driver, so the `bash -n`
check and the single re-exec per pass are part of the carry. [implemented: a568a2e12]

Triage (s4, 2026-10-23 07:10Z, tick_loop.sh stale checkout, accepted, narrowed), verbatim:
Detect that the checkout is behind origin/main and restart between passes; never fast-forward in place under a running relay.

Measured facts: #2626's head moved 4 times because a 30 h loop ran a stale cloud_relay.sh; this is the second instance of the class (P4, 2026-10-21, was closed as "restart after a merge that touches tick_loop.sh or cloud_relay.sh"), and the recurrence that decision named. A fast-forward of the checkout each pass is unsound at origin/main tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh: the loop is a bash script read incrementally and it detaches cloud_relay.sh (RELAY_HOLDER, header lines 1-22), so rewriting either file while it runs corrupts the pass or a relay in flight, and a dirty or branch-checked-out tree makes the ff fail or move a branch. R10-ORCH-MACHINERY, the earlier candidate, is absorbed and is not valid.
Mechanism: each pass, `git fetch -q origin main` (git, not API), count `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main -- tools/audit/seat tools/pr tools/audit/carry_audit.py` (only the paths the loop runs); above 0 print a `TICK-STALE <utc> behind=<n>` banner on the pass line; above a bound N (default 25 commits, or any change to tick_loop.sh or cloud_relay.sh themselves) and with no relay in flight (the flock is free) and a clean detached tree, `git checkout -q --detach origin/main` and exec the new tick_loop.sh with the same args; otherwise refuse the pass with rc and the banner. The restart point is between passes, never mid-relay.
Alternatives rejected: R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN (M), R10-ORCH-BEATD (L; its supervised beat may replace the loop, so the check moves with the loop and BEATD's brief should say so). This group already edits relay_start in tick_loop.sh (P15), so the check lands in the same file without a second PR.
Cost: S-M, about 30-50 lines in tick_loop.sh plus self-test rows with a stub git: behind-by-0 passes silently; behind with a tick_loop.sh change and no relay in flight restarts; a relay in flight (lock held) does not restart; a dirty tree refuses and prints the banner, never ff. One mutant per row (file-scoped ids tick_loop-N). [implemented: a568a2e12]

groups.brief: Third instance of the class one unretried GitHub read kills an instrument, together with P7's record_row.py HTTP 500: an audit-class barrier. adopt as an audit-class barrier in new fly-in R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY (S, lane F, priority HIGH: it sits on the merge path), in two PRs ordered by file overlap. Do not fold into R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN, which is unregistered and a much larger mechanisation. (1) Third instance of the class "one unretried GitHub read kills an instrument", measured. Across every train log since 2026-10-20 there are 11 TRAIN STOPPED lines, and 2 are transient reads: train 8's `approve: ... could not read pull request #2547` (train2547/state8, 21:50:38Z, after waiting t+2667 s for CI, with 7 entries released) and `ci: the head commit at <sha> could not be read: Get "https://api.github.com/...": net/http...` in merge_train.py's own read. Add P7's record_row.py `HTTP Error 500` on main's push run, whose revisit trigger ("a second 5xx instance") is now met. The remaining 9 stops are content refusals (red CI 3, HOLDER worktree 4, stale carry 1, ledger merge 1), so 18% of train stops are pure transport. (2) The cause and the precedent. app_approve.sh l.104 `js=$(gh api "repos/$1/pulls/$2") || die` has three sibling reads (l.271 comments, l.406 CODEOWNERS, l.408 files), all single-shot, discarding stderr so the failure class is lost. app_push.sh already holds the house pattern (l.188-251: bounded RB_SLEEP*3^(n-1), 5/15/45 s, transport refusals distinguished from a genuine refusal, never retry-forever). Reuse that rule rather than inventing 10/30/60. (3) Classification, so it cannot mask a refusal. Retry only network/transport errors, HTTP 5xx, and 429 or a secondary-rate-limit 403 (honouring Retry-After). Anything else (401, 403-permission, 404, 422, or a body that parses but is wrong: head moved, no verdict, owned path) refuses at once, as today. After the budget it refuses with the last error text kept. Mutation-write calls (review POST, merge) are never retried by this rule; they keep their own guarded paths. (4) Ordering. PR 1, app_approve.sh's four reads plus self-test arms: no open PR or live handoff touches tools/pr/app_approve.sh, so dispatch now, ahead of R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT (P17, same file), which gains an after-edge on it. PR 2, merge_train.py's GitHub reads and record_row.py's urlopen: after #2585 (CI-LAYOUT-P1: merge_train.py, record_row.py), #2584 (MAIN-GATE: merge_train.py) and #2524 (PUSHER-REAP: merge_train.py). Cost: ~25 lines in bash, ~20 in python, one shared rule stated once in INSTRUMENTS.md. Benefit: about 45 min of CI wait plus a relaunch for each transient stop (2 in about 30 h of trains), and one red main push run per 5xx. (5) Null control, in each self-test: a stub `gh` failing once with a transport error then answering passes, with exactly 2 calls logged. A stub answering 404, or a head mismatch, refuses after exactly 1 call (no retry masks a refusal). A stub failing 4 times refuses after the budget, naming the last error. A stub answering 500 to record_row twice then 200 records. Brief addition: "bounded retry of GitHub READS only, app_push.sh's 5/15/45 s rule, retrying transport errors, 5xx, 429 and secondary-limit 403 and nothing else; fixtures: one transient then success (2 calls), 404 and a wrong head (1 call, immediate refuse), budget exhausted (refuse with the last error); PR 1 is app_approve.sh, PR 2 is merge_train.py and record_row.py after #2585, #2584 and #2524".

Each card gives its destination in brackets, then the change.

- G1 Meta-work budget [R11 playbook + D13 amended]: cap the machinery share of dispatched groups or seat-hours (about 40%). When the budget is spent, new instrument groups freeze; the exception is a group whose pre-registered metric removes measured toil. Cap fly-in inflow.   - Tier 0 (record/roster/triage): deterministic checks only.
  - Tier 1 (non-gating tools, docs): a rubric review.
  - Tier 2 (custom_components, gate/merge/stamp/approval instruments): the full fixer/fix-review protocol.

- G3 Parallel-candidate pilot [R11 playbook]: covers the next 6 L/XL product groups, or any product group after its second real-class block. Two independent fixers work from the approved design note. Choose mechanically: mutants killed, then the finder's harness at both ends, then the archscore delta. Only the winner is reviewed. Pre-registered against 22.5% yield / 2.9 verdicts. Small design seat for the selection rule.
- G4 Reviewer calibration [D13 amended + R11 playbook]: each round, a blind judge on a different model re-adjudicates about 30 blocks (stratified by class) plus about 20 merge verdicts at the same heads. Publish the false-block and missed-defect rates and set a precision floor. The labels feed G5.
- G5 Contract regression evals [R11 playbook + D11 amended]: a frozen set of 30-50 labelled historical PR heads (labels from G4). A fix-review.md or COMMON.md change runs k=3 and reports precision, recall and pass^k. A fixer.md change runs on 5-10 seeded tasks. D11: a contract change without an eval result is a finding. Design seat; depends on G4.
- G6 Ratchet the machinery [D7 amended + R11 playbook]: one-sided caps on tools/ at current values (max file LOC, max function LOC/CC, duplication). Extend archscore counters to tools/; D7 audits the machinery. Design seat for the archscore part only.
- G7 Pre-registered process changes [R11 playbook + D13]: triage accepts only with a metric, a baseline instrument, a review date and a revert criterion. At most about 5 unvalidated process changes run at once. D13 reports closed vs open loops.
- G8 Rule-enforcement registry [R11 playbook + D11 amended]: every must/never rule gets an id mapped to its enforcing check, or marked judgement. Enforced rules' prose moves into the check's refusal message. Role briefs keep only the judgement rules. D11 audits coverage. Design seat.
- G9 Token/cost telemetry [R11 playbook + D13]: a ledger from seat transcripts and cloud run logs, by group, stage and model. Report tokens per merged product PR, per real catch, and per standing-seat hour.
- G10 One tool surface [R11 playbook]: a single `hpo <noun> <verb>` entry point with uniform --json, exit codes and idempotency keys. INSTRUMENTS.md is generated from it. Migrate the most-used paths first. Design seat first; phased.

- the merge train;
- the writer/reviewer split with a frozen head;
- state outside the context window;
- one-sided policy caps;
- RCA triggers;
- null controls;

findings: nightly-status NIGHTLY ABSENT misdiagnoses a workflow younger than its first cron slot
groups.brief: nightly-status (tests/nightly_status.py, classify(), the ABSENT arm around l.346) turns every PR head and main red with 'NIGHTLY ABSENT: no scheduled run of the workflow was found at all ... GitHub disables schedules on repositories with no recent activity'. Measured 2026-10-22: nightly.yml (cron '17 2 * * *') reached main with #2585 (fae523a14, 08:05Z), after that day's 02:17Z slot; `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/workflows/nightly.yml` gives state=active, created 2026-10-22T08:05:56Z; `actions/workflows/nightly.yml/runs?event=schedule` total_count 0. So the schedule is NOT disabled: the workflow is younger than its first slot, and the message's stated cause is false. Every PR must answer the red in its body until the first scheduled run (pr-contract refused #2622 for it). Fix: distinguish (a) no cron slot has elapsed since the workflow reached main (read the workflow's created_at, or the first-parent commit that added the file, against the cron) -> a NEW/PENDING state that is not red, bounded to the first slot plus a grace (the cron period plus one hour), after which ABSENT reds as today; (b) the workflow's state is disabled_* -> ABSENT with GitHub's own reason (one read of actions/workflows/<file>); (c) active and past its first slot with no run -> ABSENT, worded without the inactivity claim. Keep classify() pure: new inputs are data, drivable from tests/entities.py. Controls: a fixture workflow created after the last slot reads NEW, not red; the same fixture 26 h later with no run reads ABSENT (null control: the grace does not hide a dead schedule); GitHub's disabled-for-inactivity workflow state reads ABSENT with that reason. Mutants: drop the grace bound -> the 26 h fixture passes wrongly; drop the state read -> the disabled fixture loses its reason. Spare the API: at most one extra read per run. If the first scheduled Nightly (due ~2026-10-23T02:17Z) lands before this merges, the fix still stands for the next new scheduled workflow (CI-LAYOUT P2b adds more).

`bus.sh confirm` must refuse a replay before it moves a ref. `confirm()` pushes the verdict commit through `append_commit` (the `git push` at line 266) and only then reaches `post_verdict`, whose `posted-signed` test (line 340) refuses a tree already posted. On 2026-10-25 a double confirm of #2753 at r2 pushed a second signed commit (2974f78b6, same tree) to `verdict/2753` and then refused to post it, so the ref tip no longer matched the posted comment 6399353335 and the merge train refused the PR; the repair was a lease-protected force push. Move the check ahead: after `tree` is computed in `confirm()`, refuse when `<pr> <tree>` is in `$S/posted-signed`, with the existing `BUS refused <pr> <c>: this signed verdict was already posted on #<pr> (a replay)` text, before `append_commit`. Controls: a second confirm of an already-posted tree exits nonzero and `verdict/<pr>` still points at the first commit (null: a first confirm on a new tree pushes and posts once); a confirm of a new round's distinct tree still posts; one mutant that restores the push-first order. When `open_pr.sh` opens the PR, the dispatch record is re-keyed to the PR number, and the relay posts the held verdict on the PR. The train's existing `app_approve.sh --carry <verdict> <PR head>` decides whether it stands: a clean main merge carries (line 243), the row commit carries once P123 lands, and anything else returns to review as today. The row-before-review ordering note (`bus.sh:22-32`) becomes row-before-merge. The policy text follows in the same PR: `standing-dispatch.md`'s dispatch moment and `fix-review.md` step 7 (owner-raised V55 under mandate 6329234399). Evidence: handoff-to-open median 0.99 h, mean 2.54 h (plan-opt card V53). Controls: a handoff-dispatched verdict whose PR head is the handoff tip plus a clean main merge carries and posts (null: a PR head with a conflict resolution refuses the carry and the PR is re-dispatched at its head); a verdict for a topic that never opens a PR is reported, never posted; one mutant that posts without the carry check fails the conflict arm. carry: Lean flow study alignment (STUDY K17), binding on the build. The flow groups add work the approved design's beat and ledger must own, and they land first, so build them in: (0) The beat and every job it runs are detached processes, never an agent loop: in the live run of 2026-10-21, agent-based relay and tick loops ended their turns twice and had to be re-armed. beatd.py runs under daemonize.py and an operating-system supervisor that restarts it (launchd on the orchestrator's Mac, a user systemd unit elsewhere); an agent only reads beatd status and the journal, and never hosts a job. Jobs run concurrently: one job's run never delays another job's schedule, so a long handoff update (9 min observed on 2026-10-21) never leaves the tick board stale; the tick reads independently of the relay, as R10-TICK-RELAY-DECOUPLE (#2549) already does for tick_loop.sh. The handoff job honours R10-FLOW-RELAY-HOLD's hold file. (1) beatd.jobs.json gains two jobs: heartbeat (R10-FLOW-ANDON's job script; interval 300 s, timeout 60 s; its ref message carries beatd status, so a timed-out job alerts the owner, not only a dead host) and pitch (R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN's job script; on the hour or when the previous train ends; it only launches a detached train and reads the train-stop obligation, never waits on CI). (2) The ledger gains one event kind, postmerge-owed (producer: R10-FLOW-POSTMERGE's after-merge step; closer: that step's later success or an orchestrator disposition), because the design refuses an OWED shape with no ledger kind. (3) The handoff job carries R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY's body-only path unchanged and writes a disposition for the handoff-body ref it applies; it also does not move any pull request head while that pull request has a live reviewer in workers.json, which generalises R10-FLOW-ROSTER-FREEZE's predicate from the roster pull request to every head (fixer.md's freeze, made mechanical). (4) The seats job reads the dispatch records R10-FLOW-DISPATCH writes through bus.sh dispatch, which also gives the folded dispatch reason the round-3 review's N11-R found has no backing state. (4b) The ledger's verdict-unposted obligation closes only on a read-back: the posted pull request comment fetched and its first line matching the verdict and head, as comment-readback.md requires; a relayed claim that a verdict was posted is not a close (revision 8, observed live). (5) Is-main-red has one owner, the classifier #2570 and R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE share; the tick and the sweep do not grow a third. (6) The plan page: if R10-PLAN-ARTIFACT (#2558) merges first, part (3) extracts plan_model() from its code rather than building a second page, keeps the UNAVAILABLE page and the five mutation fixtures, and renders R10-FLOW-BOARD's flow section from the same model. (7) Inventory row M43 is stale: pr_cap.py gates dispatch, not opening, since #2525. From triage P236 (V150, orchestrator s10, 2026-10-28): extend this group's single-instance lock to the orchestrator session itself. On resume, before its first dispatch, the session takes a lock record holding its own long-lived pid (the session binary, never the calling shell's $PPID, which dies with the call) and its start time. Owner request (tvofi, 2026-10-24), issue #2733: three routing invariants hold at every roster state. (1) Every carry not yet implemented routes to a roster group that is not done. (2) Every live roster group lists at least one issue in `issues` or `fixes`. (3) Every open issue but #201 is listed by at least one live roster group. Extend the instruments, add no script; size S, per the verifier (the verifier report filed on #2733, section 5). (a) roster_edit.py gains `mark-carry <group> <index|--match TEXT> implemented <sha>|moved <GROUP>|dismissed <reason>`; carry_audit.py gains an offline `roster` subcommand that REPORTS STRANDED = a pending carry on a done group; legacy carries (existing on done groups at the cut-over roster sha) are exempt, so there is no blanket migration and nothing is marked implemented by default. `[implemented: <sha>]` records that the sha is on main; it is not verification. (b) roster_sync sets the existing `carries-open` stage instead of `done` when pending carries remain; no set-stage refusal, so the factual sync at every merge is unchanged. (c) Invariant 2 is a brief_lint warning, not an error, so roster_edit's --push lint gate and fly-in registration at dispatch are not blocked. Invariant 3 is a tick report line in the default pass from the tick's cached issue list (CARRY made default and offline); the issue check is report-only on push, with no failing CI job on issues. Wire it in `.claude/settings.json` as a PreToolUse hook with matcher `Bash`. Model it on `pre-edit.sh`: the payload is passed as an argument, the hook fails open on anything it cannot parse, and it exits 2 only on a positive match. - First, a bash `case` prefilter exits 0 on any payload without the substring `kill`. Measured: about 3 ms per call against about 26 ms for a python start. - Then it reads `tool_input.command` and refuses at command position (line start, or after `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `$(`, a backtick, `sudo`, `xargs` or `env`) each of: - `pkill` with any arguments; - `killall`; - `kill` fed by `pgrep`. - Heredoc bodies are not read. - The refusal names the preamble rule and the alternative (`$!` or a pidfile). (2) Fix `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`'s hooks check (`cmdHooks`). It tests every PreToolUse matcher against its list of edit tools only, so it would report this hook's `Bash` matcher as `MATCHER BLIND`. Key the tool set on the hook script instead: `pre-edit.sh` keeps the edit tools, and the Bash hook is tested against `Bash`. Add the Bash hook to its `REQUIRED` list. (3) Self-test rows: - Refused: - `pkill -f ""`; - `pkill -f tests/entities.py`; - `pkill python3`; - `killall python3`; - `kill $(pgrep -f x)`; - `pgrep -f x | xargs kill`; - `cd /tmp && pkill -f x`; - `sudo pkill x`. - Allowed: - `kill 1234`; - `kill $!`; - `kill $(cat run.pid)`; - `grep -n pkill file`; - `git log --grep=killall`; - `echo "never pkill"`; - a heredoc whose body holds `pkill -f x`; - `git status`, which takes the prefilter path. (4) Mutants: - Drop the command-position anchor, and the `grep -n pkill` row fails. - Drop the `killall` arm, and its row fails. - Drop the pgrep-feed arm, and the `xargs kill` row fails. - Make `policy_lint`'s matcher test edit-only again, and it reports `MATCHER BLIND`. (5) Classify the new script for `tests/entities.py`. (6) Ownership and effect. `.claude/hooks/` and `.claude/settings.json` are code-owned (`@tvofi`), so the PR merges on tvofi's approving review or under mandate 6329234399. A local seat loads hooks from the checkout it runs in, so the hook protects local seats only once the orchestrator advances that checkout. Cloud seats get it from their fresh checkout, and a cloud seat's kill reaches only its own container, so the exposure is the shared local host. The interim, the orchestrator's call: this host already runs user-level PreToolUse Bash hooks outside the tree (the main-checkout guard), and the same script installed there protects every local seat at once, before the checkout advances. Not in scope: the `pkill` mentions in prose in `tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py` and `tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh`, which are rules, not calls. triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch86.md#P323 [moved: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE]

- Map a seat branch to its PR topic; a merged or closed PR makes the seat eligible, once it has no unpushed commits, a clean status and no live process.
- Read the seats root from config or the environment.
- Add a class for plain copies under a seat dir whose topic's PR is merged.

groups.brief:
Programme-closeout work, and it runs LAST: after R10-ARCH-DOCS and R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK have merged, after the roster and the state docs have moved into main, and before the closure stamp. Owner request (tvofi, 2026-10-24): the programme must contain a group that cleans up after itself and drives the open branches down to the owner's 1-3 target. Round-10 end state: main plus at most two development branches, remote and local, every other ref archived as a tag first, GitHub's merged pull request branches already deleted. This group is the single owner of that end state; R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS owns only the two defects in tools/audit/seat/prune_refs.py and must land first, so this group uses prune_refs.py as its ref instrument and never a session-local loop (decision 0013).

Deliver a self-tested closeout instrument under tools/audit/seat/ that composes the existing instruments (tools/audit/seat/prune_refs.py, tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh, tools/audit/seat/state_docs.py) and is a dry plan by default, acting only under --apply, with the ordering below written as code. Then run it with --apply as the final act of the round (the orchestrator's step; the pull request lands the instrument and its fixtures, the run leaves the end state and the report). Steps, each gated by the one before:
(1) Move the roster and the state docs into main, because the roster branch and the state ref are read at run time and must not be deleted while a workflow or a citation reads them (see the R9-CLOSURE-BRANCHES brief in dev/programme/rosters/wave-r9-groups.json for the hazard list). Sweep in-tree citations of every ref family about to go and retarget each to the archive tag at the same sha; prove it with node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs (dev/governance/rules/brief-citations.md).
(2) Archive before delete: every remaining handoff/*, handoff-body/*, fix/*, design/*, review/*, probe/*, claim/*, dispatch/* and record/* ref (and the other families prune_refs.py enumerates, verdict/* only once --verdicts-drained) is retagged under archive/<family>/<name> at its own commit, then its branch is deleted. origin keeps main plus at most two branches. Derive the counts with git ls-remote and a prefix histogram; carry none.
(3) Local state: remove every seat worktree under ~/hpo-seats and under ~/.local/state/hpo/pr (a worktree holding an unpushed commit is reported and kept until the owner rules; worktree_gc.sh must already leave such a worktree alone, which is R10-FLY-WORKTREE-GC); clear scratch under ~/hpo-orch except the final ledger and state; prune git worktrees; reduce local branches to main plus at most two; run a final worktree_gc.
(4) Issues and sessions: close or disposition every open issue except the coordination issue's successor, each with the number that closes it or the re-scope that keeps it; archive merged cloud sessions.
(5) Closure report: write counts before and after for refs by family, tags added, worktrees, local branches, open issues and open pull requests, plus every ref left and the rule that kept it, to the round-10 evidence directory under dev/audit/rounds/.
Controls: a fixture where a ref to be deleted lacks its archive tag must refuse (every tag precedes every delete); an open-PR ref and main are kept (null control); a worktree with an unpushed commit survives; a dry run writes nothing. Spare the API: batch ref writes (R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS carry (i)). Part of #201.

groups.brief: Proposed new fly-in group R10-IMMERSION-LATCH (size S). No roster group mentions immersion, booster or resistive heat. From D15 triage (2026-10-24; derived ratios only). The owner has no immersion element, yet October books an immersion line equal to 3.9 % of the month's metered kWh (absent in August and September), with 7 latch events in the thermal store between 10-18 and 10-20, all at DHW times. Seams. (1) `_detect_immersion` (custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py:8838-8895) latches on two samples where the measured draw exceeds `max_electrical_power` x `IMMERSION_FACTOR` (1.15, const.py:1156) while the plan commands heat. On this install that is the pump's own meter, which also carries its built-in DHW booster or backup heater (both entities are configured), or a compressor drawing above the configured 4.0 kW nameplate. Either way it is not an immersion element, and nothing checks that one is configured: `immersion_feedback_enabled` is False. (2) While latched, `_accumulate_energy` (coordinator.py:10201-10214) books as immersion everything the meter drew above the PLAN's ask (`actual_power_kw - planned_total`), not above the nameplate threshold that tripped the latch. The plan under-reads this pump's draw 1.28x on running steps, so ordinary compressor draw is carved out as resistive heat for every interval of the latch, including the two clear samples needed to release it. Effect on savings: none in total. `savings_actual` is the full metered energy and the carve-out only relabels the spot line. Correction to carry-d15-sav-volume-2: the immersion kWh is not a separate appliance missing from the baseline; it is part of the same metered-versus-modelled volume gap. Fix: label the excess by its source (the pump's booster or backup flag when configured; immersion only when an element is configured); measure the excess over the latch threshold, not over the plan; and refuse the line on an install with no resistive element configured. Controls: a synthetic install without an element that draws 2x its ask books no immersion; one with a configured booster books only the excess over nameplate while the flag is on; the null of flat draw at or below nameplate books zero; one mutant.

Two items bind this group before any fixture is committed:
(1) RECORDER READER. export.py reads the recorder that `recorder: db_url` names, not just `<config>/home-assistant_v2.db`. MySQL/MariaDB is the case to cover; PostgreSQL is optional. The rules:
- It takes the URL from configuration.yaml, resolving `!secret` through secrets.yaml, or from `--db-url`.
- It never prints, logs or writes the URL's credentials.

- It uses a driver the Home Assistant container already ships, found at runtime with a refusal that names it, so the SQLite path stays stdlib-only.

- An id that maps to no role becomes a stable hash-derived id.
- Friendly names and any other free text are dropped, not masked.
- seal() refuses a document still holding an unmapped id, or any token that looks like a street address, a word followed by a house number. Fixture-driven tests cover both refusals.
- The real address must never appear in any tracked file, test, fixture, body, commit message, ref or report. Test data uses invented names only, e.g. "Exempelgatan 12". Do not echo the owner's real entity ids into scratch output that reaches a report.

carry: tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py: take the approval's review-event CI run off the merge's critical path. Every `app_approve.sh` approval starts a `CI review pr=<n>` run of `ci.yml` (`pull_request_review`), and the merge is refused by base-branch policy until that run concludes: runs of 66 s, 74 s and 76 s for #2709, #2741 and #2710 on 2026-10-24. `land` then pays two refused 30-s attempts, about 1.8 min per merge. (1) Approve each entry once its head is fixed at admission, while the proof or the earlier entries' merges run, not inside `land` just before the merge. (2) Post no second approval when the approver's APPROVED review already sits at exactly that head: `app_approve.sh` always POSTs, and #2741 was approved twice around a `[MAIN-MOVED]` re-prove, starting a second review run. A head that moved still gets a fresh approval at its new head. (3) Before the first merge attempt, wait for the head's review-event run to conclude, instead of the blind 30-s retry grain (a poll on the check-runs at the head, or `mergeStateStatus`). Controls: in a batch of 2 or more, every entry's approve-to-merge gap is under 20 s and its refused-attempt count is 0; one review run per entry per head; the null is a single-entry batch approved inside `land` (today's path), which still shows about 70 to 110 s. The train undrafts a head it has already proved mergeable, instead of stopping on it (P218/V138, owner-directed V131; from #2854 sitting green on every check but `BLOCKED`/`REVIEW_REQUIRED` only because `isDraft` was true, hours as the v7.0.5 critical path, and #2878 admitted as a draft and undrafted 23 s later). In `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`'s merge step, where a refusal would stop, run `gh pr ready <n>` -- but only on a head the train has already admitted to that step, meaning ALL of: a posted `merge` verdict naming the current head or one `app_approve.sh --carry` says carries to it; a clean merge tree against main; a delivery row at the head; no failing or pending required context; and the approval the step posts. NARROWING (this ruling): undraft only when the head was **recorded as a draft at admission** -- record `draft: true` at `add` (V130's add-time note) and compare at the merge step -- so a head an author drafts AFTER admission to hold it is left alone; the five conditions cannot see intent, the recorded boolean can see that one act. Undrafting writes no commit and moves no head, so the verdict still names the tree being merged. Log one `UNDRAFT #<pr> <head>` line; re-read `isDraft` after the call and continue to the merge only if it is false (a re-draft between call and merge stops the run); a failed `gh pr ready` is a `Stop` with its own phase, never a silent continue. Null controls: a non-draft head at the same step behaves identically with no `UNDRAFT` line; a draft whose verdict names an older head is not undrafted; a draft with a pending required context is not undrafted; a head drafted after admission is not undrafted. Fixer's change under the fix protocol: failing test on a draft head first, then review. The space-step classifier labels a heating step preheat_weather whenever the step's heat-loss factor exceeds 1.1, and it tests this before the price test. That factor includes the learned house_heat_loss_scale, so a house whose learned scale is above 1.1 is labelled "preheat for weather" under perfectly flat weather. Measured, flat weather and flat price: scale 1.05 gives 0 such steps; scale 1.2356 gives 51; the owner's live plan gave 88 of 96.

Fix: test only the forecast's weather component, meaning the factor relative to its own scale-free baseline, so a learned level never reads as weather.
Controls:
- flat weather with scale 1.24 gives zero preheat_weather steps;
- a real forecast cold spell, at scale 1.0 and at 1.24, still labels preheat_weather;
- null control: scale 1.0 with flat weather is unchanged.
One mutant: revert to the raw factor; it fails the first control. [implemented: d7582ed404a87603bd02fefda610d7ebbe4181e1]

Instance: #2856 at b6de9fad, about 3 h at REVIEW_REQUIRED, nightly run 40300518367 skip-train-hold; it was worked around by a hand approval (review 5650544835). Change: move the hold block to after the approver App's review and before THE PITCH. A held beat runs the guard, dismisses on refusal, posts the one approving review per head, and exits skip-train-hold without merging. No change to merge_train.py. Update the nightly.yml comments that state the order. Controls, over tests/entities.py's executed _train_hold_status harness: a live hold with the guard passing returns skip-train-hold, records the approver POST and no merge (the existing 'skips while a live merge train holds' check moves to guard_rc=0 and gains these assertions); a live hold with the guard refusing returns refused, dismisses and posts no review; the pitch check's live-hold arm keeps skip-train-hold; no hold reaches the pitch and merge as today (null); one mutant moving the hold back ahead of the approval fails the 'reviewed under a live hold' assertion. The filed alternative, the train posting the approver review itself, is REJECTED: a second approval site, the approver key in the train, and a hot file. groups.brief: Make the owner's 2026-10-27 ruling mechanical: a head that carries no code change keeps its review, and no seat has to judge which moves those are. THE RULE. The test is a commit range, not an opinion: git rev-list --count <reviewed-head>..<new-head> --not origin/main. Zero, or a count whose commits are all merges of origin/main, means no branch-authored change and the prior merge verdict carries. Any non-merge commit in that range means the head carries code and takes a fresh review. A body rewrite never by itself voids a verdict. A claim-file resolution inside a merge IS a change, so the range is read before the merge is trusted. THE WORK. groups.brief: Hotfix from a live user finding (tvofi, 2026-10-30, #201 comment 6528614583): with away mode on, the plan kept heating slots. The investigation probe's report is BODY.md at handoff-body/r10-live-away-heating aa6e5db30ba6fe7cb4a2f1016c271ae9bf260af2; read it in full. Its harness is carried in that report. Defect measured there: while away and not recovering, away.solve_bands sets target_temp, min_temp and the day and night comfort fields to the away target, but not the weekend comfort fields or the holiday comfort fields. So the optimizer's per-step comfort pair (the weekend and holiday branches of _comfort_pair in optimizer.py) replaces the away setback on Saturdays, Sundays and holiday dates: Saturday comfort reads 21.0 where it should read 16.0. Fix: in away.solve_bands, while away and not recovering, also set comfort_temp_day_weekend, comfort_temp_night_weekend, holiday_comfort_day and holiday_comfort_night to the away target wherever they are configured. Extend the away module's field tuple and setback-config protocol to match. Failing test first, in tests/features.py, through solve_bands and the optimizer's comfort-bounds builder, never a re-implemented formula. Controls: the weekend and holiday arms read Saturday comfort equal to the away target; null control: away off keeps the weekend and holiday values; recovery_active keeps today's behaviour, which drops the setback (whether it should is a design question for tvofi, not this fix). One mutant per added field. Commit the probe's harness as a new file in the harnesses directory under dev/audit, named after the probe topic, classified in tests/closure.py, and run it at both ends: before, the weekend and holiday rows read Sat 21.0; after, 16.0; every other row is unchanged. No goldens are expected to move. Out of scope: a state listener on the away presence entity, which belongs to R10-LIVESTATE's coordinator move. Its finding is carried there.

groups.brief: Owner request, 2026-10-30 (tvofi): the Home Assistant Marketplace repository page does not show the front-page README graphics. Pre-study at handoff-body/r10-readme-graphics, measured against homeassistant 2026.11.0b1 and home-assistant-frontend 20261028.1. Its core finding: the Marketplace sanitizer (js-xss safeAttrValue in the frontend markdown worker) blanks every src and href that is not absolute and does not start with ./ or ../ or /, before its URL rewriter runs. So every repository-relative image and link in README.md renders broken, and mermaid fences show as plain code. (1) Prefix every repository-relative link and image target in README.md with ./ so GitHub, tools/site/build_docs.mjs and the Marketplace all resolve it. (2) For each mermaid block in README.md, commit a pre-rendered PNG (2x, opaque, light) rendered with the mermaid pinned in tools/site through Chromium on the pattern of docs/img/readme/render.mjs. Place it as a ./ markdown image directly above the block, and close that block's details element. The setup-flow block stays identical to docs/configuration.md and docs/setup.md. (3) Add an arm to tests/doc_claims.py that refuses a bare-relative src, href or srcset in README.md, and refuses a mermaid block whose figure is missing or whose recorded source hash (a sidecar manifest the generator writes) differs from the block. Show a planted one-character block edit red, a planted prefix removal red, and the unchanged tree green. (4) Classify the new manifest and figures as reads of tests/doc_claims.py in tests/closure.py, the route docs/img/brand/coffee.svg took. Finder's harness: a replica of the Marketplace markdown pipeline under dev/audit/harnesses/, red at the base and green at the head, with an absolute-URL image as the null control. Dark mode is IN scope (tvofi, 2026-10-30: "dark mode should absolutely not be scoped out. you have your mandate"). Each figure also gets a dark PNG and is placed as a picture element with a prefers-color-scheme dark source and a light img fallback. The Marketplace replica shows what the picture element renders there, and the drift arm requires both variants. Out of scope: docs other than README.md, VERSION and release notes. Must merge before R10-ARCH-DOCS and R10-CATALOG-PR: the Marketplace fetches README.md at the release tag, so only a stamped release shows the fix.

groups.brief: Measure-first hotfix from a live user finding (tvofi, 2026-10-30). The owner's two-zone house plans about 67 kWh of space heat a day at 20-22 C indoor and about 6 C outdoor. The owner moved T6 from indoor to lower floor. Void the affected learner's evidence on an entity-id change, through the same path as the basis voiding in the house-heat-loss re-anchor. Failing tests first, through the production coordinator, never a re-implemented formula. Defect, measured twice on 2026-10-30 (19:2xZ and 21:2xZ): the detached state_docs.py beat died with roster_edit.Refuse from fetch_origin in tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py. Its git fetch of every origin head into refs/remotes/origin failed with 'cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/train-hold: is at X but expected Y', because another process sharing the repository's refs (the merge train, the tick, a seat) moved that remote-tracking ref between the fetch's read and its write. The same race refused the roster seat's own op (set-stage R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY, refused rc=2 on 'cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/wip-sync/...'), so every roster_edit caller shares it, not only the beat. One lost race in a shared clone kills a long-running beat or refuses a roster op, and the orchestrator restarts it by hand. Fix at the seam that owns it: fetch_origin (or run) treats a ref-lock race as transient and retries with a short backoff, bounded, and still refuses on any other failure. Alternatively, the beat's loop survives one failed pass and retries on its next interval. Pick one and say why. Controls: a test that simulates the lock-race stderr shows the retry succeeds; a non-race failure still refuses; a race that persists past the bound still refuses (no infinite loop). The state_docs beat must outlive an injected single lock race. Measure the retry bound against the real collision rate, using the beat's log.

groups.brief: From triage P323 (orchestrator s8, 2026-10-31): a seat ran `pkill -f` with an empty pattern while restarting its watch loop. The 2026-10-15 instance (#2216's fixer, `pkill -f tests/entities.py`) killed every seat's run of that script. The seat preamble and the memory note both forbid it, so the rule is in process state (b). (1) Add a new hook script beside `.claude/hooks/pre-edit.sh`, the Bash hook. Wire it in `.claude/settings.json` as a PreToolUse hook with matcher `Bash`. Model it on `pre-edit.sh`: the payload is passed as an argument, the hook fails open on anything it cannot parse, and it exits 2 only on a positive match. - First, a bash `case` prefilter exits 0 on any payload without the substring `kill`. Measured: about 3 ms per call against about 26 ms for a python start. - Then it reads `tool_input.command` and refuses at command position (line start, or after `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `$(`, a backtick, `sudo`, `xargs` or `env`) each of: - `pkill` with any arguments; - `killall`; - `kill` fed by `pgrep`. - Heredoc bodies are not read. - The refusal names the preamble rule and the alternative (`$!` or a pidfile). (2) Fix `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`'s hooks check (`cmdHooks`). It tests every PreToolUse matcher against its list of edit tools only, so it would report this hook's `Bash` matcher as `MATCHER BLIND`. Key the tool set on the hook script instead: `pre-edit.sh` keeps the edit tools, and the Bash hook is tested against `Bash`. Add the Bash hook to its `REQUIRED` list. (3) Self-test rows: - Refused: - `pkill -f ""`; - `pkill -f tests/entities.py`; - `pkill python3`; - `killall python3`; - `kill $(pgrep -f x)`; - `pgrep -f x | xargs kill`; - `cd /tmp && pkill -f x`; - `sudo pkill x`. - Allowed: - `kill 1234`; - `kill $!`; - `kill $(cat run.pid)`; - `grep -n pkill file`; - `git log --grep=killall`; - `echo "never pkill"`; - a heredoc whose body holds `pkill -f x`; - `git status`, which takes the prefilter path. Hotfix from a live user defect. Live user finding (tvofi, 2026-10-30). Probe report: handoff-body/r10-live-plan-energy 7c4e639e49214592ef2ef2ddd48df522a3efd2cd, measured at main cc930cdd1.

The space-step classifier labels a heating step preheat_weather whenever the step's heat-loss factor exceeds 1.1, and it tests this before the price test. That factor includes the learned house_heat_loss_scale, so a house whose learned scale is above 1.1 is labelled "preheat for weather" under perfectly flat weather. Measured, flat weather and flat price: scale 1.05 gives 0 such steps; scale 1.2356 gives 51; the owner's live plan gave 88 of 96.

Fix: test only the forecast's weather component, meaning the factor relative to its own scale-free baseline, so a learned level never reads as weather.
Controls:
- flat weather with scale 1.24 gives zero preheat_weather steps;
- a real forecast cold spell, at scale 1.0 and at 1.24, still labels preheat_weather;
- null control: scale 1.0 with flat weather is unchanged.
One mutant: revert to the raw factor; it fails the first control.
